prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1233; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a left-turn collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck by an oncoming vehicle at an intersection. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver, with coverage active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Police report obtained, and it places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Statements from two independent witnesses match the described sequence of events.

Entry 4: Scene photographs and the other driver's account both confirm the collision occurred as reported. Vehicle damage is largely consistent with the described impact, though the impact appears to have been light.

Entry 5: Medical records received showing a wrist fracture. The injury is severe relative to the low-speed contact visible in the photos, and the reported mechanism does not readily explain it.

Entry 6: Records show the treatment followed a typical course, with care tapering as the claimant's condition improved. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the available history.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in each conversation with the adjuster and through counsel. No inconsistencies have been noted to date.

Entry 8: Reviewed the vehicle's prior claim history and found no earlier damage on record. Preliminary repair estimate is being compared against the photos for further review.

Entry 9: File is pending a final evaluation of the injury claim against the medical records and the light-impact findings. Counsel has been notified that a decision on the bodily injury portion will follow the review.
